summary: aiosendletter exfiltrates Windows LOCALAPPDATA\logs to a hardcoded Cloudflare Worker and attempts UAC elevation
details: The package's init() function archives the contents of %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs into a ZIP via shutil.make_archive and POSTs it to a hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Worker endpoint (https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/) using requests.post with a 'document' file field. Before performing the upload, init() invokes ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW with the 'runas' verb to relaunch sys.executable with the current argv under admin rights, prompting the user for UAC elevation and re-executing the exfiltration path with elevated privileges. The pyproject.toml description labels the package a 'Safe bug reporter for sending local logs via Cloudflare Workers' and declares a bogus 'ctypes' PyPI dependency; the self-declared 'bug reporter' purpose is the cover for unattended bulk upload of a Windows user's application-data directory to a third-party host controlled by the author.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
